meaning:
ἀνα-λαμβάνω
[in LXX chiefly for נָשָׂא, also for לָקַח, etc. ;]
1. to take up, raise: Mrk.16:19, Act.1:2, 11 1:22 10:16, 1Ti.3:16.
2. to take up, take to oneself: Act.7:43 20:13-14 23:31, Eph.6:13, 16, 2Ti.4:11 (for late exx., v MM, VGT, see word).†
(AS)

renderings.bsb: He was taken up to heaven

elsewhere.note: until the day in which he was received up, after he had given commandment through the Holy Spirit to the apostles whom he had chosen.
Therefore put on the whole armor of God, that you may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand.
Without controversy, the mystery of godliness is great: God was revealed in the flesh, justified in the spirit, seen by angels, preached among the nations…
Only Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for service.
